title: Trademark Protection for Cashew Processing and Packaged Food Brands in Kollam
metaTitle: Cashew & Food Brand Trademark Protection in Kollam | BRNDNUR
metaDescription: Intellectual property strategy for Kollam cashew processors and food brands under Nice Class 29, 30, and 35. Protect your export identity and consumer packaging.
intendedAudience: Cashew factory owners, nut packaging brand founders, agro-exporters, and dry fruit distributors in Kollam, Kilikollur, and Ayathil.
quickAnswer: Cashew processors and packaged food brands in Kollam must register their brand names and packaging graphics under Nice Class 29 (covering processed, roasted, salted, and packaged nuts). Expanding into flavored nut snacks or confectionery also requires Class 30, while wholesale export trading services require Class 35. Trademarks protect export value and prevent counterfeit packaging in domestic and Gulf markets.

h2Sections.h2: The Evolution of Kollam’s Historic Cashew Processing Industry
content: Kollam has been the global epicenter of cashew kernel processing for nearly a century, centered around processing clusters in Kilikollur, Ayathil, and Kundara. Historically, local processors operated primarily as bulk wholesale suppliers shipping unbranded 50-pound tins to international brokers.

Today, competitive market dynamics have compelled Kollam processors to transition toward value-added retail packaging—launching roasted, flavored, organic, and gift-packed cashew products sold under proprietary consumer brands across India and the GCC diaspora.

h2Sections.h2: Nice Classification for Cashew & Nut Ventures
content: To ensure airtight intellectual property coverage, cashew enterprises must classify their operations accurately across product and service classes:

rows: Processed nuts, roasted cashews, salted nuts, flavored nuts, cashew butter, edible oils.
Vacuum-packed plain cashew kernels (W180, W210, W240, W320), roasted & salted cashews, peri-peri cashews, cashew paste.
Confectionery, chocolate-coated nuts, cashew sweets (Kaju Katli), baked nut snacks.
Chocolate-enrobed cashews, traditional cashew halwa, nut cookies, seasoned flour-coated nut snacks.
Raw, unprocessed agricultural products, raw in-shell cashew nuts.
Raw cashew nuts (RCN) imported directly from West Africa or domestic orchards prior to factory processing.
Wholesale, retail, e-commerce, and export trading services for dry fruits and nuts.
Cashew retail showroom chains, dry fruit online web portals, export trading agency services.

content: In the retail dry fruit market, counterfeiters frequently copy the overall look and feel ("trade dress") of premium tins, pouches, and gift boxes. Registering a **Device Mark** or **Label Mark** under Class 29 protects the distinctive visual layout, color combinations, and typography of your retail packaging.
Under the Trade Marks Act, a label registration gives you the legal authority to seize counterfeit packaging through civil injunctions and police raids under Section 115.
checklist: Wordmark Registration: Protects the brand name itself in all trade formats.
Label / Device Registration: Protects your signature tin, pouch, or gift-box design.
FSSAI Number Integration: Mandatory display of the 14-digit FoSCoS license on the front of all commercial nut packaging.

faqs.question: Does registration with the Cashew Export Promotion Council (CEPCI) grant trademark protection?
faqs.answer: No. CEPCI provides export promotion, quality standards, and trade facilitation. It does not confer intellectual property ownership. Only an IP India registration under the Trade Marks Act 1999 gives statutory brand exclusivity.

faqs.question: Can I register grade names like "Kollam W180"?
faqs.answer: No. Grade designations like "W180" or "W240" are generic industry standards describing kernel size and cannot be monopolized. Your trademark must be a distinctive proprietary name (e.g., "Royal Cashews") placed above the grade descriptor.
